study type: Prospective combined with retrospective observational cohort study
outcome: favorable cervix (Bishop score >= 6) 24 h after cervical ripening
mean induction time to vaginal delivery
cohort: The study participants were obese women (pre-pregnancy BMI > 30 kg/m2) at term (> 37 weeks) with live singleton fetuses in vertex presentation and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score < 6) undergoing labor induction.
finding: For obese patients at term, cervical ripening using a double-balloon catheter is more efficient in achieving a favorable Bishop score after 24 hours compared to vaginal dinoprostone.
mod_finding: No significant difference was observed in the cesarean section rate or the mean induction time to vaginal delivery between the double-balloon catheter and dinoprostone groups.
